```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
```

# Overview

Denoising pipeline (DADA2 → phyloseq) for the **Jeppe-Bac** run: 26 paired-end
samples (JOS-Bac1..26), bacterial V3–V4 (Bac341F/805R), sequenced on a
**MiSeq i100**.

Because the i100 uses **XLEAP-SBS 2-colour chemistry** with **RTA4 binned
Q-scores**, three settings differ from a classic MiSeq pipeline:

1. **No `truncLen`** — quality stays high to the read end; use `minLen`.
2. **`rm.lowcomplex`** — 2-colour chemistry can miscall no-signal as high-Q
   "G", creating poly-G runs that distort the error model.
3. **Binned error model** — `makeBinnedQualErrfun()` instead of the default.

*(Source: `MiSeqi100_dada2_error_correction.pdf`.)*

```{r packages}
rm(list = ls())

setwd("C:/Users/jeppe/Desktop/Bioinf/MiSeq_8_7")
## Packages ##
library(BiocParallel)

## Force Bioconductor functions to run serially on Windows ##
BiocParallel::register(BiocParallel::SerialParam(), default = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = 1)

library(dada2)
library(phyloseq)
library(Biostrings)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

## Confirm ##
BiocParallel::bpparam()

```

# Paths and file names

```{r paths}

# the 52 .fastq.gz live here
path <- file.path("FH_raw")
filt.dir <- file.path("filtered_FH")
out.dir  <- file.path("results_FH")
fig.dir  <- file.path("figures_FH")    # all plots exported here as PNG
dir.create(filt.dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(out.dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(fig.dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Helper: display a ggplot AND save it to figures/ (300 dpi).
# Works both interactively (console) and when knitting.
save_fig <- function(p, name, w = 8, h = 5) {
  ggsave(file.path(fig.dir, name), plot = p, width = w, height = h,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  p   # return so it also prints
}

fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern = "_R1.fastq.gz", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern = "_R2.fastq.gz", full.names = TRUE))
# Sample name = Bac#_S###  (drop "JOS-" prefix, join the Bac token + S token)
# e.g. "JOS-Bac1_S146_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz" -> "Bac1_S146"  (matches metadata.csv)
parts <- strsplit(basename(fnFs), "_")
sample.names <- sapply(parts, function(x) paste0(sub("^JOS-", "", x[1]), "_", x[2]))
stopifnot(length(fnFs) == length(fnRs))
sample.names

length(fnFs)
length(fnRs)

basename(fnFs)
basename(fnRs)

all(file.exists(fnFs))
all(file.exists(fnRs))

file.info(fnFs)$size
file.info(fnRs)$size
```

# Sample display order and labels

another. The matching set is selected automatically from the FASTQ sample names,

# Read quality and complexity {.tabset}

MiSeq i100 profiles look flat/high (mostly Q38) and banded (binning) — that is
normal and is why we do not truncate.

## Forward quality
```{r qc-fwd}
save_fig(plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:2]), "01_arch_quality_forward.png", w = 9, h = 5)
```

## Reverse quality
```{r qc-rev}
save_fig(plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:2]), "02_arch_quality_reverse.png", w = 9, h = 5)
```

## Complexity (poly-G check)
Random sequence → ~16; poly-G → ~1. A peak near 1 means `rm.lowcomplex` (next
step) will strip those reads.
```{r qc-complex}
save_fig(plotComplexity(fnFs[1:2]), "03_arch_complexity_forward.png", w = 9, h = 5)
save_fig(plotComplexity(fnRs[1:2]), "04_arch_complexity_reverse.png", w = 9, h = 5)
```

# Filter and trim

Primers (still on reads): **Bac341F** `CCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG` (17 bp) /
**Bac805R** `GACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC` (21 bp) → `trimLeft = c(17, 21)`.
MiSeq i100: `minLen` instead of `truncLen`, plus `rm.lowcomplex`.

```{r filter}
filtFs <- file.path(filt.dir, paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path(filt.dir, paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
names(filtRs) <- sample.names

out <- filterAndTrim(
  fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs,
  minLen = 200,
  maxN = 0, maxEE = c(2, 2), truncQ = 2,
  rm.phix = TRUE, rm.lowcomplex = 8,
  compress = TRUE
)
out
```

> **JOS-Bac26 (S164)** is tiny (~59 KB) — almost certainly a negative control.
> Expect very few reads; keep it here to check contamination, drop before diversity.

# Error model (binned Q-scores) {.tabset}

```{r errors}
BinnedErrfun <- makeBinnedQualErrfun(c(2, 12, 24, 38))
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, errorEstimationFunction = BinnedErrfun)
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, errorEstimationFunction = BinnedErrfun)
```

## Forward errors
```{r err-fwd}
# flat line in the empty low-Q range is expected (no data in those bins)
save_fig(plotErrors(errF, nominalQ = TRUE), "05_arch_errors_forward.png", w = 8, h = 7)
```

## Reverse errors
```{r err-rev}
save_fig(plotErrors(errR, nominalQ = TRUE), "06_arch_errors_reverse.png", w = 8, h = 7)
```

# Denoise, merge, ASV table, chimeras

```{r denoise}
dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err = errF)
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err = errR)

mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs, verbose = TRUE)

seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab)))   # merged-length distribution (V3-V4 ~400-430)

seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method = "consensus", verbose = TRUE)
cat("Dimensions (samples x ASVs):", dim(seqtab.nochim), "\n")
cat("Fraction reads kept after chimera removal:",
    round(sum(seqtab.nochim) / sum(seqtab), 3), "\n")
```

# Read tracking (QC)

Big drops at any single step point to a parameter problem.

```{r track}
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))
track <- cbind(out,
  denoisedF = sapply(dadaFs, getN),
  denoisedR = sapply(dadaRs, getN),
  merged    = sapply(mergers, getN),
  nonchim   = rowSums(seqtab.nochim))
colnames(track)[1:2] <- c("input", "filtered")
rownames(track) <- sample.names
write.csv(track, file.path(out.dir, "read_tracking.csv"))
track
```

# Taxonomy

Taxonomy is assigned with the DADA2-formatted training FASTA specified below.
The downstream table keeps six taxonomic ranks through genus.

```{r taxonomy}

## GTDB r226 bacterial representative SSU training set ##
## Taxonomy is restricted to Domain -> Genus ##

gtdb.train <- "GTDB_r226_ar53_reps_DADA2_genus_trainset.fa.gz"

## Assign taxonomy ##
taxa.out <- assignTaxonomy(
  seqtab.nochim,
  gtdb.train,
  taxLevels = c(
    "Domain",
    "Phylum",
    "Class",
    "Order",
    "Family",
    "Genus"
  ),
  outputBootstraps = TRUE,
  multithread = 4,
  verbose = TRUE
)

## Taxonomy matrix ##
taxa <- taxa.out$tax

## Naive-Bayes bootstrap confidence (%) per rank ##
boot <- taxa.out$boot
colnames(boot) <- paste0(colnames(boot), " (BS)")

## Inspect taxonomy ##
taxa.print <- taxa
rownames(taxa.print) <- NULL

head(taxa.print)
```

# phyloseq object

Build the phyloseq object used in the downstream analysis and attach the ASV
sequences. Sample names are kept identical to `sample.names`.

```{r phyloseq}
## Ensure sample names are correct ##
rownames(seqtab.nochim) <- sample.names

ps <- phyloseq(
  otu_table(seqtab.nochim, taxa_are_rows = FALSE),
  tax_table(taxa)
)

## Add ASV sequences ##
dna <- DNAStringSet(taxa_names(ps))
names(dna) <- taxa_names(ps)
ps <- merge_phyloseq(ps, dna)

## Rename taxa to ASV1, ASV2, ... ##
taxa_names(ps) <- paste0("ASV", seq_len(ntaxa(ps)))

saveRDS(ps, file.path(out.dir, "phyloseq_gtdb.rds"))
ps <- readRDS("results_FH/phyloseq_gtdb.rds")

ps

# ============================================================
# COMMUNITY COMPOSITION
# ============================================================


## ============================================================
## CLEAN PHYLOSEQ OBJECT
## ============================================================

## Keep Bacteria and Archaea ##
ps <- subset_taxa(
  ps,
  Domain %in% c(
    "Bacteria",
    "Archaea"
  )
)


## Remove taxa without assigned phylum ##
ps <- subset_taxa(
  ps,
  !is.na(Phylum) &
    !Phylum %in% c(
      "",
      "NA"
    )
)


## Remove taxa with zero abundance ##
ps <- prune_taxa(
  taxa_sums(ps) > 0,
  ps
)


sort(
  sample_sums(ps)
)

## ============================================================
## GENERAL RELATIVE-ABUNDANCE FUNCTION
## ============================================================

## Show every taxon reaching >= min_pct in ANY sample.
## Taxa below the threshold are collapsed into one grey block.
## Unassigned genera remain their own category.

rel_abund_bar <- function(
    ps,
    level = "Genus",
    min_pct = 1
) {

  ## Convert whole community to relative abundance ##
  rel <- transform_sample_counts(
    ps,
    function(x) x / sum(x)
  )


  ## Agglomerate at requested taxonomic rank ##
  g <- tax_glom(
    rel,
    taxrank = level,
    NArm = FALSE
  )


  ## Convert to dataframe ##
  df <- psmelt(g)

  df[[level]] <- as.character(
    df[[level]]
  )


  ## Keep unassigned taxa explicitly ##
  df[[level]][
    is.na(df[[level]])
  ] <- "Unassigned"


  ## Sample ordering ##
  df$Sample <- factor(
    df$Sample,
    levels = order
  )


  ## Maximum abundance reached by each taxon ##
  mx <- tapply(
    df$Abundance,
    df[[level]],
    max
  )


  ## Taxa reaching threshold in at least one sample ##
  keep <- names(mx)[
    mx >= min_pct / 100
  ]


  ## Order by mean abundance ##
  ord <- names(
    sort(
      tapply(
        df$Abundance,
        df[[level]],
        mean
      ),
      decreasing = TRUE
    )
  )


  keep <- ord[
    ord %in% keep
  ]


  if (length(keep) > length(tax_pal)) {

    warning(
      length(keep),
      " taxa >= min_pct but only ",
      length(tax_pal),
      " palette colours; raise min_pct or extend tax_pal."
    )
  }


  rare <- paste0(
    "<",
    min_pct,
    "%"
  )


  df$Taxon <- factor(
    ifelse(
      df[[level]] %in% keep,
      df[[level]],
      rare
    ),
    levels = c(
      keep,
      rare
    )
  )


  ## One block per taxon ##
  df <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample + Taxon,
    df,
    sum
  )


  ## Assign colours ##
  fills <- c(
    setNames(
      tax_pal[
        seq_along(keep)
      ],
      keep
    ),
    setNames(
      "#c4c3bb",
      rare
    )
  )


  ## Plot ##
  ggplot(
    df,
    aes(
      Sample,
      Abundance,
      fill = Taxon
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.95,
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = fills
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      labels = samlabels
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) x * 100,
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Relative abundance (%)",
      fill = level
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 90,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 0.5
      ),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(
        0.42,
        "cm"
      ),
      legend.text = element_text(
        size = 8
      )
    )
}

  "Methylosarcina"       = "#BCBD22",
  "Methylosoma"          = "#E377C2",
  "Methylomarinum"       = "#393B79",
  "Methylotetracoccus"   = "#637939",
  "Methylospira"         = "#8C6D31",
  "Methyloparacoccus"    = "#843C39",
  "Methylogaea"          = "#3182BD",
  "Methylocucumis"       = "#31A354",
  "Methylohalobius"      = "#756BB1",
  "Methylothermus"       = "#E6550D",
  "Crenothrix"           = "#6BAED6",
  "Clonothrix"           = "#74C476",
  "Methylocella"         = "#FD8D3C",
  "Methylocapsa"         = "#9ECAE1",
  "Methyloferula"        = "#A1D99B",
  "Methylovirgula"       = "#F768A1",
  "Methylorosula"        = "#08519C",
  "Methylacidiphilum"    = "#54278F",
  "Methylacidimicrobium" = "#006D2C",
  "Methylomirabilis"     = "#CB181D"
)



## ============================================================
## METHYLOTROPH COLOURS
## ============================================================

## These colours are also unique, but the strongest colour
## separation is intentionally reserved for the methanotrophs.

## ============================================================
## METHYLOTROPH COLOURS
## ============================================================

methylotroph_pal <- c(
  "Methylobacterium"    = "#8DD3C7",
  "Methylorubrum"       = "#FB8072",
  "Methylophilus"       = "#80B1D3",
  "Methylotenera"       = "#FDB462",
  "Methylobacillus"     = "#B3DE69",
  "Methylovorus"        = "#FCCDE5",
  "Methyloversatilis"   = "#BC80BD",
  "Methylibium"         = "#CCEBC5",
  "Methylopila"         = "#FFED6F",
  "Methylophaga"        = "#1F9E89",
  "Methylorhabdus"      = "#F46D43",

  ## Hyphomicrobium GTDB genera kept separate ##
  "Hyphomicrobium"      = "#5E4FA2",
  "Hyphomicrobium_A"    = "#B15928",
  "Hyphomicrobium_B"    = "#6A3D9A",
  "Hyphomicrobium_C"    = "#FF1493",

  "Ancylobacter"        = "#3288BD",
  "Xanthobacter"        = "#ABDDA4",
  "Paracoccus"          = "#FDAE61",
  "Acidomonas"          = "#D53E4F",
  "Amycolatopsis"       = "#9E0142"
)



## ============================================================
## COMBINED FUNCTIONAL PALETTE
## ============================================================

functional_pal <- c(
  mob_pal,
  methylotroph_pal
)


## Check that no genus has accidentally been assigned twice ##
if (anyDuplicated(names(functional_pal))) {

  stop(
    "Duplicate genus names occur in functional_pal."
  )
}


## Check that no exact colour is reused ##
if (anyDuplicated(unname(functional_pal))) {

  warning(
    "At least one exact colour is reused in functional_pal."
  )
}



## ============================================================
## HELPER FUNCTION FOR FIXED COLOURS
## ============================================================

get_functional_fills <- function(genera) {

  genera <- as.character(
    genera
  )


  ## Identify any genus for which no colour has been defined ##
  missing_colours <- setdiff(
    genera,
    names(functional_pal)
  )


  if (length(missing_colours) > 0) {

    stop(
      paste0(
        "No fixed colour defined for: ",
        paste(
          missing_colours,
          collapse = ", "
        ),
        "\nAdd these genera to functional_pal before plotting."
      )
    )
  }


  ## Return colours in the requested genus order ##
  functional_pal[genera]
}



## ============================================================
## METHANOTROPH REGEX
## ============================================================

## Matches the base genera plus GTDB suffixes such as:
##
## Methylobacter
## Methylobacter_A
## Methylobacter_C
##
## They remain separate taxa after matching.

mob_regex <- paste0(
  "^(",
  paste(
    aerobic_mob_genera,
    collapse = "|"
  ),
  ")(_[A-Z0-9]+)?$"
)



## ============================================================
## METHYLOTROPH REGEX
## ============================================================

methylotroph_regex <- paste0(
  "^(",
  paste(
    methylotroph_genera,
    collapse = "|"
  ),
  ")(_[A-Z0-9]+)?$"
)



# ============================================================
# METHANOTROPHS AS % OF WHOLE COMMUNITY
# ============================================================


## Convert entire community to relative abundance FIRST ##
rel_all <- transform_sample_counts(
  ps,
  function(x) x / sum(x)
)


## Convert to dataframe ##
mob_df <- psmelt(
  rel_all
)


mob_df$Genus <- as.character(
  mob_df$Genus
)


## Keep methanotroph genera ##
mob_df <- mob_df[
  !is.na(mob_df$Genus) &
    grepl(
      mob_regex,
      mob_df$Genus
    ),
]


## Remove unwanted samples ##
mob_df <- mob_df[
  !mob_df$Sample %in% c(
    "JO-Bac6_S74",
    "JO-Bac7_S75",
    "JO-Bac8_S76",
    "Bac22_S160",
    "Bac23_S161",
    "Bac24_S162",
    "Bac25_S163"
  ),
]


## Preserve desired sample order ##
mob_df$Sample <- factor(
  mob_df$Sample,
  levels = order
)



if (nrow(mob_df) == 0) {

  message(
    "No methanotroph genera detected in these samples."
  )

} else {


  ## ==========================================================
  ## COLLAPSE ASVs TO GENUS
  ## ==========================================================

  mob_df <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample + Genus,
    mob_df,
    sum
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## ORDER LEGEND BY MEAN ABUNDANCE
  ## ==========================================================

  ## This changes ONLY the legend order.
  ## It does NOT affect genus colours.

  ord <- names(
    sort(
      tapply(
        mob_df$Abundance,
        mob_df$Genus,
        mean
      ),
      decreasing = TRUE
    )
  )


  mob_df$Genus <- factor(
    mob_df$Genus,
    levels = ord
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## GET FIXED GENUS COLOURS
  ## ==========================================================

  fills <- get_functional_fills(
    ord
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## PLOT
  ## ==========================================================

  p_mob <- ggplot(
    mob_df,
    aes(
      Sample,
      Abundance,
      fill = Genus
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.9,
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = fills
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) x * 100,
      expand = c(
        0,
        0.01
      )
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      labels = samlabels
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Relative abundance (% of community)",
      fill = "Methanotroph genus"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 1,
        margin = margin(t = 2)
      ),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(
        0.42,
        "cm"
      ),
      legend.text = element_text(
        size = 8
      )
    )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## SAVE FIGURE
  ## ==========================================================

  save_fig(
    p_mob,
    "09_FH_gtdb_relabund_methanotrophs.png",
    w = 7,
    h = 5
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## TOTAL METHANOTROPH ABUNDANCE TABLE
  ## ==========================================================

  tot <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample,
    mob_df,
    sum
  )


  tot$Percent <- round(
    100 * tot$Abundance,
    3
  )


  write.csv(
    tot[
      ,
      c(
        "Sample",
        "Percent"
      )
    ],
    file.path(
      out.dir,
      "methanotroph_total_percent.csv"
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )


  print(
    tot[
      ,
      c(
        "Sample",
        "Percent"
      )
    ]
  )


  plot(
    p_mob
  )
}



# ============================================================
# WITHIN-METHANOTROPH COMMUNITY
# ============================================================


## Identify methanotroph ASVs ##
mob_taxa <- grepl(
  mob_regex,
  as.character(
    tax_table(ps)[
      ,
      "Genus"
    ]
  )
)


mob_taxa[
  is.na(mob_taxa)
] <- FALSE



if (!any(mob_taxa)) {

  message(
    "No methanotroph genera detected in these samples."
  )

} else {


  ## ==========================================================
  ## KEEP ONLY METHANOTROPH TAXA
  ## ==========================================================

  ps_mob <- prune_taxa(
    mob_taxa,
    ps
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## NORMALISE WITHIN METHANOTROPH COMMUNITY
  ## ==========================================================

  ## Samples containing no methanotroph reads remain zero
  ## rather than producing NaN values.

  ps_mob <- transform_sample_counts(
    ps_mob,
    function(x) {

      if (sum(x) == 0) {

        return(x)

      }

      x / sum(x)
    }
  )


  ## Convert to dataframe ##
  win_df <- psmelt(
    ps_mob
  )


  ## Remove unwanted samples ##
  win_df <- win_df[
    !win_df$Sample %in% c(
      "JO-Bac6_S74",
      "JO-Bac7_S75",
      "JO-Bac8_S76",
      "Bac22_S160",
      "Bac23_S161",
      "Bac24_S162",
      "Bac25_S163"
    ),
  ]


  ## Sample order ##
  win_df$Sample <- factor(
    win_df$Sample,
    levels = order
  )


  win_df$Genus <- as.character(
    win_df$Genus
  )


  ## Collapse ASVs to genus ##
  win_df <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample + Genus,
    win_df,
    sum
  )


  ## Remove zero-abundance genus/sample combinations ##
  win_df <- win_df[
    win_df$Abundance > 0,
  ]


  ## ==========================================================
  ## ORDER LEGEND BY MEAN ABUNDANCE
  ## ==========================================================

  ord <- names(
    sort(
      tapply(
        win_df$Abundance,
        win_df$Genus,
        mean
      ),
      decreasing = TRUE
    )
  )


  win_df$Genus <- factor(
    win_df$Genus,
    levels = ord
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## SAME FIXED COLOURS AS WHOLE-COMMUNITY PLOT
  ## ==========================================================

  fills <- get_functional_fills(
    ord
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## PLOT
  ## ==========================================================

  p_win <- ggplot(
    win_df,
    aes(
      Sample,
      Abundance,
      fill = Genus
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.9,
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = fills
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) x * 100,
      expand = c(
        0,
        0
      )
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      labels = samlabels
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Relative abundance (% of methanotrophs)",
      fill = "Methanotroph genus"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 90,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 0.5
      ),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(
        0.42,
        "cm"
      ),
      legend.text = element_text(
        size = 8
      )
    )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## SAVE FIGURE
  ## ==========================================================

  save_fig(
    p_win,
    "10_FH_5_gtdb_methanotrophs_within.png",
    w = 7,
    h = 5
  )


  ## ==========================================================
  ## COMPANION TABLE
  ## ==========================================================

  win_wide <- reshape(
    transform(
      win_df,
      Percent = round(
        100 * Abundance,
        3
      )
    )[
      ,
      c(
        "Sample",
        "Genus",
        "Percent"
      )
    ],
    idvar = "Sample",
    timevar = "Genus",
    direction = "wide"
  )


  names(win_wide) <- sub(
    "^Percent\\.",
    "",
    names(win_wide)
  )


  write.csv(
    win_wide,
    file.path(
      out.dir,
      "methanotroph_within_percent.csv"
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )


  print(
    win_wide
  )


  plot(
    p_win
  )
}

## ============================================================
## METHANOTROPH + METHYLOTROPH COMMUNITY
## ============================================================

## Convert WHOLE community to relative abundance first ##
rel_all <- transform_sample_counts(
  ps,
  function(x) x / sum(x)
)


## Convert to dataframe ##
functional_df <- psmelt(rel_all)

functional_df$Genus <- as.character(
  functional_df$Genus
)


## ============================================================
## IDENTIFY FUNCTIONAL GROUP
## ============================================================

functional_df$Functional_group <- NA_character_


## Methanotrophs ##
functional_df$Functional_group[
  !is.na(functional_df$Genus) &
    grepl(
      mob_regex,
      functional_df$Genus
    )
] <- "Methanotroph"


## Methylotrophs ##
functional_df$Functional_group[
  !is.na(functional_df$Genus) &
    grepl(
      methylotroph_regex,
      functional_df$Genus
    )
] <- "Methylotroph"


## Keep only selected functional taxa ##
functional_df <- functional_df[
  !is.na(functional_df$Functional_group),
]


## Remove unwanted samples if required ##
functional_df <- functional_df[
  !functional_df$Sample %in% c(
    "JO-Bac1_S69", 
    "JO-Bac2_S70", 
    "JO-Bac3_S71",
    "JO-Bac4_S72", 
    "JO-Bac5_S73",
    "Bac22_S160",
    "Bac23_S161",
    "Bac24_S162",
    "Bac25_S163"
  ),
]


## Preserve sample order ##
functional_df$Sample <- factor(
  functional_df$Sample,
  levels = order
)



## ============================================================
## COLLAPSE ASVs TO GENUS
## ============================================================

functional_df <- aggregate(
  Abundance ~ Sample + Genus + Functional_group,
  functional_df,
  sum
)



## ============================================================
## CHECK COLOURS
## ============================================================

present_genera <- unique(
  functional_df$Genus
)

missing_colours <- setdiff(
  present_genera,
  names(functional_pal)
)

if (length(missing_colours) > 0) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "No fixed colour defined for: ",
      paste(
        missing_colours,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}



## ============================================================
## COLLAPSE LOW-ABUNDANCE GENERA (<1% IN ALL SAMPLES)
## ============================================================

min_pct <- 1

other_label <- "Other methano- and methylotrophs (<1%)"

## Maximum relative abundance per genus across samples
genus_max <- functional_df %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(
    Max_abundance = max(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Keep genera reaching at least 1% in any sample
keep_genera <- genus_max %>%
  filter(Max_abundance >= min_pct) %>%
  pull(Genus)

## Collapse everything else
functional_df <- functional_df %>%
  mutate(
    Genus = if_else(
      Genus %in% keep_genera,
      Genus,
      other_label
    ),
    Functional_group = if_else(
      Genus == other_label,
      "Other",
      Functional_group
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sample, Genus, Functional_group) %>%
  summarise(
    Abundance = sum(Abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## ============================================================
## ORDER GENERA
## ============================================================

genus_order <- functional_df %>%
  group_by(Genus, Functional_group) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_abundance = sum(Abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Functional_group = factor(
      Functional_group,
      levels = c(
        "Methanotroph",
        "Methylotroph",
        "Other"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Functional_group,
    desc(Total_abundance)
  ) %>%
  pull(Genus)

functional_df$Genus <- factor(
  functional_df$Genus,
  levels = genus_order
)

## ============================================================
## COLOURS
## ============================================================

fills <- c(
  functional_pal[
    setdiff(genus_order, other_label)
  ],
  setNames(
    "#B3B3B3",
    other_label
  )
)
## ============================================================
## PLOT
## ============================================================

p_functional <- ggplot(
  functional_df,
  aes(
    Sample,
    Abundance,
    fill = Genus
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.9,
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fills
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) x * 100,
    expand = c(
      0,
      0.01
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = samlabels
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Relative abundance (% of community)",
    fill = "Genus"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      margin = margin(t = 2)
    ),
    legend.key.size = grid::unit(
      0.42,
      "cm"
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 8
    )
  )


plot(
  p_functional
)


save_fig(
  p_functional,
  "methanotrophs_methylotrophs.png",
  w = 8,
  h = 6
)


```

# Community composition {.tabset}

```{r clean}
## Keep Bacteria/Archaea with assigned phylum ##
ps <- subset_taxa(
  ps,
  Domain %in% c("Bacteria", "Archaea")
)

ps <- subset_taxa(
  ps,
  !is.na(Phylum) & !Phylum %in% c("", "NA")
)

ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)

sort(sample_sums(ps))
```


`rel_abund_bar()` agglomerates at the chosen rank and shows **every taxon that
reaches `min_pct`% in at least one sample as its own named bar** — so real genera
are never hidden inside a generic "Other". `Unassigned` (no genus in GTDB) is
kept as its own honest category. Only the genuinely negligible tail (each taxon
< `min_pct`%) collapses into a single grey `<min_pct%` block; each bar still sums
to 100%.

At `min_pct = 1` these 4 samples show ~13 genera. Note: past ~8 hues, colours are
no longer all colour-blind-distinct, so identity leans on the legend + the white
segment gaps. Lowering `min_pct` reveals more taxa but pushes colour reuse
further (there are 101 genus-level groups here, ~87 of them < 1%).

```{r relabund-fn}
# Distinct palette for up to 16 named taxa. The first 8 are the validated
# colour-blind-safe set; the rest extend it (less CVD-separated — lean on the
# legend). Grey (#c4c3bb) is reserved for the "<min_pct%" remainder.
## ============================================================
## HIGH-CONTRAST DISTINCT TAXON PALETTE
## ============================================================

## Designed for categorical separation.
## Grey (#c4c3bb) is still reserved separately for the "<min_pct%" group.
tax_pal <- c(
  "#E69F00", # orange
  "#56B4E9", # sky blue
  "#009E73", # bluish green
  "#F0E442", # yellow
  "#0072B2", # blue
  "#D55E00", # vermillion
  "#CC79A7", # reddish purple
  "#000000", # black
  "#66C2A5", # teal
  "#FC8D62", # salmon
  "#8DA0CB", # lavender blue
  "#E78AC3", # pink
  "#A6D854", # lime green
  "#FFD92F", # mustard
  "#E5C494", # tan
  "#B3B3B3", # medium gray
  "#1B9E77", # dark teal
  "#D95F02", # dark orange
  "#7570B3", # purple
  "#E7298A", # magenta
  "#66A61E", # green
  "#E6AB02", # goldenrod
  "#A6761D", # brown
  "#666666", # dark gray
  "#A6CEE3", # pale blue
  "#1F78B4", # strong blue
  "#B2DF8A", # pale green
  "#33A02C", # strong green
  "#FB9A99", # light red
  "#E31A1C", # strong red
  "#FDBF6F", # peach
  "#FF7F00"  # vivid orange
)

# Show every taxon reaching >= min_pct in ANY sample as its own bar; taxa below
# that (each individually tiny) collapse into one "<min_pct%" block. Unassigned
# (no genus in GTDB) is kept as its own category.
rel_abund_bar <- function(ps, level = "Genus", min_pct = 1) {
  rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(x) x / sum(x))
  g   <- tax_glom(rel, taxrank = level, NArm = FALSE)
  df  <- psmelt(g)
  df[[level]] <- as.character(df[[level]])
  df[[level]][is.na(df[[level]])] <- "Unassigned"
  df$Sample <- factor(df$Sample, levels = order)
  mx   <- tapply(df$Abundance, df[[level]], max)              # peak abundance per taxon
  keep <- names(mx)[mx >= min_pct / 100]
  ord  <- names(sort(tapply(df$Abundance, df[[level]], mean), decreasing = TRUE))
  keep <- ord[ord %in% keep]                                 # kept taxa, abundance-ordered
  if (length(keep) > length(tax_pal))
    warning(length(keep), " taxa >= min_pct but only ", length(tax_pal),
            " palette colours; raise min_pct or extend tax_pal.")
  rare <- paste0("<", min_pct, "%")
  df$Taxon <- factor(ifelse(df[[level]] %in% keep, df[[level]], rare),
                     levels = c(keep, rare))
  df <- aggregate(Abundance ~ Sample + Taxon, df, sum)       # one block per taxon (no striping)
  fills <- c(setNames(tax_pal[seq_along(keep)], keep), setNames("#c4c3bb", rare))
  ggplot(df, aes(Sample, Abundance, fill = Taxon)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.95, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = samlabels) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance (%)", fill = level) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, margin = margin(t = 2)),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.42, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
}
```

### Phylum (overview)
```{r relabund-phylum, fig.height=6}
save_fig(rel_abund_bar(ps, level = "Phylum", min_pct = 1),
         "07_arch_gtdb_relabund_phylum.png", w = 7, h = 6)
```

### Genus (detail)
```{r relabund-genus, fig.height=7}
save_fig(rel_abund_bar(ps, level = "Family", min_pct = 1),
         "08_arch_gtdb_relabund_family.png", w = 9, h = 7)
```

# Methanotroph / ANME genus subset

The original script contained both an aerobic MOB list and an ANME list assigned
to the same object. To preserve the behaviour of the original code, the aerobic
MOB list is retained as a reference object, while `mob_genera` remains the ANME
list that was active after the overwrite.

The abundance plots below are therefore calculated from the active
`mob_genera` list as a fraction of the whole community.

```{r methanotroph-list}
## ============================================================
## FIXED METHANOTROPH COLOUR MAPPING
## ============================================================

mob_master_genera <- c(
  "Methylicorpusculum",
  "Methylococcus",
  "Methylocaldum",
  "Methylomonas",

  "Methylobacter",
```

```{r methanotroph-bar, fig.height=5}
# % of the WHOLE community: transform first, then keep MOB genera.
rel_all <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(x) x / sum(x))
mob_df <- psmelt(rel_all)
mob_df$Genus <- as.character(mob_df$Genus)
mob_df <- mob_df[!is.na(mob_df$Genus) & grepl(mob_regex, mob_df$Genus), ]
mob_df <- mob_df[!mob_df$Sample %in% c("JO-Bac6_S74", "JO-Bac7_S75", "JO-Bac8_S76", "Bac22_S160", "Bac23_S161", "Bac24_S162", "Bac25_S163"), ]
mob_df$Sample <- factor(mob_df$Sample, levels = order)
  
 if (nrow(mob_df) == 0) {
  message("No methanotroph genera detected in these samples.")
} else {

  mob_df <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample + Genus,
    mob_df,
    sum
  )

  ## Order taxa by mean abundance for the legend ##
  ord <- names(
    sort(
      tapply(
        mob_df$Abundance,
        mob_df$Genus,
        mean
      ),
      decreasing = TRUE
    )
  )

  mob_df$Genus <- factor(
    mob_df$Genus,
    levels = ord
  )

  ## Fixed colours across datasets ##
  fills <- mob_master_pal[ord]


  p_mob <- ggplot(
    mob_df,
    aes(
      Sample,
      Abundance,
      fill = Genus
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.9,
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = fills
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) x * 100,
      expand = c(0, 0.01)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      labels = samlabels
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Relative abundance (% of community)",
      fill = "Methanotroph Genus"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 90,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 0.5
      ),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.42, "cm"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8)
    )

  save_fig(
    p_mob,
    "09_FH_5_gtdb_relabund_methanotrophs.png",
    w = 7,
    h = 5
  )

  tot <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample,
    mob_df,
    sum
  )

  tot$Percent <- round(
    100 * tot$Abundance,
    3
  )

  write.csv(
    tot[, c("Sample", "Percent")],
    file.path(
      out.dir,
      "methanotroph_total_percent.csv"
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  tot[, c("Sample", "Percent")]
}

plot(p_mob)
```

## Within the selected methanotroph community

The same active genus set, but now normalised so the selected methanotroph
community sums to 100% within each sample.

```{r methanotroph-within, fig.height=5}
# Keep only MOB taxa, THEN transform so each sample's MOB sum to 1.
mob_taxa <- grepl(mob_regex, as.character(tax_table(ps)[, "Genus"]))
mob_taxa[is.na(mob_taxa)] <- FALSE

if (!any(mob_taxa)) {
  message("No methanotroph genera detected in these samples.")
} else {
  ps_mob <- prune_taxa(mob_taxa, ps)
  ps_mob <- transform_sample_counts(ps_mob, function(x) x / sum(x))   # sums to 1 per sample
  win_df <- psmelt(ps_mob)
  win_df <- win_df[!win_df$Sample %in% c("JO-Bac6_S74", "JO-Bac7_S75", "JO-Bac8_S76", "Bac22_S160", "Bac23_S161", "Bac24_S162", "Bac25_S163"), ]
  win_df$Sample <- factor(win_df$Sample, levels = order)
  win_df$Genus <- as.character(win_df$Genus)
  win_df <- aggregate(Abundance ~ Sample + Genus, win_df, sum)        # one block per genus
  ord <- names(sort(tapply(win_df$Abundance, win_df$Genus, mean), decreasing = TRUE))
  win_df$Genus <- factor(win_df$Genus, levels = ord)
  fills  <- setNames(tax_pal[seq_along(ord)], ord)

  p_win <- ggplot(win_df, aes(Sample, Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.9, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = samlabels) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance (% of methanotrophs)",
         fill = "Methanotroph genus") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.42, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
  save_fig(p_win, "10_FH_5_gtdb_methanotrophs_within.png", w = 7, h = 5)

  # Companion table: each genus as % of the methanotroph community (wide).
  win_wide <- reshape(transform(win_df, Percent = round(100 * Abundance, 3))[,
                        c("Sample", "Genus", "Percent")],
                      idvar = "Sample", timevar = "Genus", direction = "wide")
  names(win_wide) <- sub("^Percent\\.", "", names(win_wide))
  write.csv(win_wide, file.path(out.dir, "methanotroph_within_percent.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  win_wide
}
```

```{r}
## Named ANME genera ##
anme_genera <- c(
  "Methanophaga",
  "Candidatus Methanophaga",
  "Methanoalium",
  "Candidatus Methanoalium",
  "Methanoxibalbensis",
  "Candidatus Methanoxibalbensis",
  "Methanospirans",
  "Candidatus Methanospirans",
  "Methanospirare",
  "Candidatus Methanospirare",
  "Methanocomedens",
  "Candidatus Methanocomedens",
  "Methanomarinus",
  "Candidatus Methanomarinus",
  "Methanogaster",
  "Candidatus Methanogaster",
  "Methanoperedens",
  "Candidatus Methanoperedens",
  "Methanovorans",
  "Candidatus Methanovorans"
)

## Exact genus matching ##
anme_regex <- paste0(
  "^(",
  paste(anme_genera, collapse = "|"),
  ")(_[A-Z0-9]+)?$"
)

## Relative abundance of whole community ##
rel_all <- transform_sample_counts(
  ps,
  function(x) x / sum(x)
)

anme_df <- psmelt(rel_all)

anme_df$Genus <- as.character(anme_df$Genus)

anme_df <- anme_df[
  !is.na(anme_df$Genus) &
    grepl(anme_regex, anme_df$Genus),
]

## ---------------------------------------------------------
## If no ANME are detected, explicitly create zero values
## ---------------------------------------------------------

if (nrow(anme_df) == 0) {

  anme_plot_df <- data.frame(
    Sample = sample_names(ps),
    Abundance = 0
  )

  anme_plot_df$Sample <- factor(
    anme_plot_df$Sample,
    levels = order
  )

  p_anme <- ggplot(
    anme_plot_df,
    aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance)
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.9,
      fill = "grey70",
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) x * 100,
      limits = c(0, 0.01),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = samlabels) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "ANME relative abundance (% of community)",
      title = "Anaerobic methanotrophic archaea",
      subtitle = "No ANME detected"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 90,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 0.5
      )
    )

} else {

  ## Normal plotting when ANME are present ##
  anme_df <- aggregate(
    Abundance ~ Sample + Genus,
    anme_df,
    sum
  )

  anme_df$Sample <- factor(
    anme_df$Sample,
    levels = order
  )

  ord <- names(
    sort(
      tapply(
        anme_df$Abundance,
        anme_df$Genus,
        mean
      ),
      decreasing = TRUE
    )
  )

  anme_df$Genus <- factor(
    anme_df$Genus,
    levels = ord
  )

  fills <- setNames(
    tax_pal[seq_along(ord)],
    ord
  )

  p_anme <- ggplot(
    anme_df,
    aes(
      Sample,
      Abundance,
      fill = Genus
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.9,
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) x * 100,
      expand = c(0, 0.01)
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = samlabels) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "ANME relative abundance (% of community)",
      fill = "ANME genus"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +

      legend.key.size = unit(0.42, "cm"),

}

## ============================================================
## SEARCH PHYLOSEQ OBJECT FOR ANME ARCHAEA
## ============================================================

## Extract taxonomy table ##
tax <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps))

## Keep ASV / OTU IDs ##
tax$ASV <- rownames(tax)


## ============================================================
## KNOWN ANME NAMES
## ============================================================

anme_terms <- c(
  "Methanophaga",
  "Methanoalium",
  "Methanoxibalbensis",
  "Methanospirans",
  "Methanospirare",
  "Methanocomedens",
  "Methanomarinus",
  "Methanogaster",
  "Methanoperedens",
  "Methanovorans",
  
  ## GTDB placeholder associated with ANME-3 ##
  "DQIP01",
  
  ## Catch explicit ANME labels if present ##
  "ANME"
)


## ============================================================
## SEARCH ACROSS THE ENTIRE GTDB LINEAGE
## ============================================================

taxonomy_columns <- setdiff(
  names(tax),
  "ASV"
)

tax$Full_taxonomy <- apply(
  tax[, taxonomy_columns, drop = FALSE],
  1,
  paste,
  collapse = "; "
)

anme_pattern <- paste(
  anme_terms,
  collapse = "|"
)

anme_taxa <- tax %>%
  filter(
    grepl(
      anme_pattern,
      Full_taxonomy,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  )


## ============================================================
## SHOW MATCHES
## ============================================================

anme_taxa %>%
  select(
    ASV,
    everything(),
    -Full_taxonomy
  )

## ============================================================
## INSPECT ARCHAEAL TAXONOMY
## ============================================================

tax <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps))
tax$ASV <- rownames(tax)

## Keep only Archaea ##
archaea_tax <- tax %>%
  filter(Domain == "Archaea")

archaea_tax

## ============================================================
## SEARCH ALL ARCHAEA FOR "METHAN"
## ============================================================

methan_tax <- archaea_tax %>%
  filter(
    if_any(
      c(Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus),
      ~ grepl("methan", ., ignore.case = TRUE)
    )
  )

methan_tax

## ============================================================
## UNIQUE ARCHAEAL TAXA
## ============================================================

archaea_tax %>%
  distinct(
    Phylum,
    Class,
    Order,
    Family,
    Genus
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Phylum,
    Class,
    Order,
    Family,
    Genus
  )

unique(archaea_tax$Order)
unique(archaea_tax$Family)
unique(archaea_tax$Genus)
```
